bill.title: Compare with your tax bill
bill.desc: Enter the amounts printed on your bill to see how far they are from this estimate and why they may differ. The closer your home, age and holding inputs match the bill, the more accurate the comparison.
bill.where: Find the comprehensive tax on your mailed or mobile bill or Hometax, and property tax in your Wetax payment history. Leave unknown fields blank.
bill.empty: Enter at least one amount from your bill to see the comparison.
bill.more: Your bill is KRW {amount} higher than the estimate
bill.less: Your bill is KRW {amount} lower than the estimate
bill.match: Your bill and the estimate are almost the same (within KRW 1,000)

why.price: Assessed price: the bill uses this year's price as of January 1. If you entered last year's price, or the price was corrected after an objection, the amount changes. Check it on Realty Price.
why.cap: Tax burden cap: any amount above 150% of last year's property tax plus comprehensive tax is removed. Enter last year's billed total in the 'last year's holding tax' field to apply it.
why.exclude: Exclusions and special rules: homes excluded as registered rentals, or covered by the temporary two-home, inherited-home or low-priced regional home rules, drop out of the home count and price total. Try entering without them.
why.joint: Joint ownership: spouses each get their own bill. The estimate is the couple's combined amount, so add both bills to compare. If you applied for the one-home special rule, only one spouse is billed.
why.oneHouse: One-home household test: if anyone in the household (spouse, family living with you) owns another home, the KRW 1.2B deduction and credits do not apply. If a special rule was approved, you are taxed as a one-home household. Match the checkbox to your bill.
why.credit: Age and holding-period credits: age is counted as of June 1, and the holding period from acquisition to June 1. Being one bracket off changes the credit a lot.
why.propDeduct: Property tax deduction: the property tax subtracted from the comprehensive tax is the amount actually levied. If your property tax came out lower than the estimate, less is subtracted and the comprehensive tax rises.
why.land: Land and other items: if the bill total includes the land portion of the comprehensive tax, or you own homes not entered here, the bill will be higher.
why.propCap: Property tax base cap: a home's property tax base cannot rise more than a set rate (up to 5%) over last year, so it can come out lower than the estimate (Local Tax Act Art. 110). Also check local reductions.
why.propExtra: Property tax bill items: July and September bills can include taxes this calculator leaves out, such as the regional resource facility tax on buildings or property tax on land.

bill.note: If the bill's facts (number of homes, household, assessed price) look wrong, check with Hometax or your tax office first. This comparison only shows the gap from an estimate with the same inputs; it does not mean your bill is wrong.

dates.notice: Bills arrive by mail or mobile in late November (in 2025, sent from November 24). Payment runs December 1-15.
dates.split: Installments: if the comprehensive tax exceeds KRW 2.5M (KRW 3M including the rural special tax), apply on Hometax or at the tax office by the due date to pay part of it by {date} with no interest.
dates.deferral: Deferral: a one-home household aged 60+ or holding 5+ years, with prior-year salary of KRW 70M or less (comprehensive income KRW 60M or less) and a comprehensive tax over KRW 1M, can apply by {date} to defer payment until the home is sold or passed on. Collateral is required and interest-equivalent charges apply when paid.
dates.special: Applications for rental exclusions, one-home special rules (temporary two homes, inherited or low-priced regional homes) and the joint-ownership special rule: {from} - {to}
dates.specialNow: The application window for exclusions and special rules is open now: {from} - {to} (Hometax or tax office)
dates.specialPassed: This year's application window for exclusions and special rules ({from} - {to}) has closed. The next one is {nextFrom} - {nextTo}. If you missed it, ask your tax office whether a December return or a correction claim can reflect it.
dates.holidayNote: If a deadline falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next business day (Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 5).

temp.contractHint: The later of the contract date and deposit payment date. By Aug 3, 2026 the comprehensive real estate tax and capital gains tax keep 3 years (transitional rule); acquisition tax keeps 3 years for contracts by Aug 26. Leave blank if unsure.
temp.title: Temporary two-home sale deadlines
temp.desc: If you bought a new home before selling the old one, each tax gives a different deadline to sell the old home. Enter the new home's acquisition date (the earlier of final payment or registration).
temp.adjusted: Both homes were in regulated areas when the new one was acquired
temp.adjustedHint: If either home is outside a regulated area, the deadline is 3 years.
temp.empty: Pick the acquisition date to see each tax's deadline.

tax.jongbu: Comprehensive real estate tax (one-home special rule)

note.jongbu: Enforcement Decree Art. 4-2. If both homes are in regulated areas and the new one was acquired on or after Aug 4, 2026, it is 2 years (from the June 1, 2027 assessment; 3 years if the contract and deposit were made by Aug 3). You must apply every Sept 16-30, and if you miss the deadline the tax saved plus interest is collected.
note.capitalGains: Income Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 155. The new home must be bought at least 1 year after the old one, and the exemption's own conditions (2-year holding, etc.) still apply. If both are in regulated areas, acquired on or after Aug 4, 2026 and sold on or after Oct 1, it is 2 years (3 years if the contract and deposit were made by Aug 3).
note.acquisition: Local Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 28-5. The rule is 3 years; the cut to 2 years when both homes are in regulated areas (acquisitions from Oct 1, 2026; 3 years for contracts by Aug 26) is based on the Ministry of the Interior's announcement, so confirm with Wetax or your local office. Missing the deadline triggers the surcharge difference.

temp.foot: Each deadline is the same calendar date N years after the new home's acquisition. Conditions differ by tax law, so confirm with a tax office or tax accountant.

u.subtitle: Enter the official assessed (gongsi) price of your homes to get your 2026 annual holding tax: property tax (July/September) plus comprehensive real estate tax (December). Includes one-home credits, joint-ownership comparison and price scenarios.

houses.title: Homes owned
houses.label: Home {n} assessed price
houses.max: You can add up to 10 homes.
houses.hint: Use the official assessed price, not the market price (look it up on realtyprice.kr). A partly owned home counts as one home.

u.oneHouseHint: The whole household owns only this home. Property tax ratio 43–45%, KRW 1.2B deduction and age/holding credits for the comprehensive tax.
u.multi: With 2+ homes: 60% property tax ratio, KRW 900M deduction and regular rates.
u.multiHeavy: With 3+ homes, the part of the tax base above KRW 1.2B is taxed at 2.0–5.0%.
u.shareHint: Spouse share {other}%. The one-home special treatment uses the larger shareholder (either one if equal).
u.urbanHint: Adds the urban-area property tax (0.14% of the tax base). Applies to most city apartments.

result.label: Annual holding tax (property + comprehensive)
result.effective: {rate}% of assessed price · about KRW {monthly} a month
result.propertyHint: Incl. urban-area tax and local education tax, paid July & September
result.jongbuHint: After property-tax offset and credits, paid in December
result.notJongbu: No comprehensive tax: assessed price is within the KRW {deduction} deduction
result.nongHint: 20% of the comprehensive tax, paid together

mode.jointEach: Joint ownership: separate KRW 900M deductions each come out lower, so they are used.
mode.jointSpecial: Joint ownership: applying the one-home special treatment (KRW 1.2B + credits) comes out lower, so it is used.

result.capApplied: The burden cap (150% of last year) reduced the comprehensive tax by KRW {amount}.
result.approx: Property tax base caps, burden caps, the regional resource facility tax and reliefs are not modelled, so your bill may differ.

share.label: Estimated holding tax this year · KRW {price} home
share.text: KRW {price} home: annual holding tax KRW {tax}

schedule.title: When you pay
schedule.julWhatAll: All property tax (KRW 200K or less, paid at once)
schedule.split: Because the comprehensive tax exceeds KRW 2.5M, KRW {amount} can be paid in installments by {date} (no interest). Apply on Hometax or at the tax office by the due date; the rural special tax is split in the same ratio.
schedule.note: Property tax is billed by the local government via Wetax; the comprehensive tax by the NTS via Hometax. Whether property tax of KRW 200K or less is billed all in July depends on local ordinance.

steps.title: How it is calculated
steps.propertyNote: Tax base = assessed price × fair market value ratio. Progressive 0.1–0.4% (one-home households with price ≤ KRW 900M: 0.05–0.35%), urban-area tax 0.14%, local education tax = property tax × 20%.

c.prop: Property tax paid on the same tax base

steps.jointNote: Sum of both spouses calculated separately (shares {shares}).

rates.title: Show comprehensive tax rates
rates.propNote: Property tax rates (on tax base): up to 60M 0.1%, 150M 0.15%, 300M 0.25%, above 0.4%. One-home (price ≤ KRW 900M): 0.05% / 0.1% / 0.2% / 0.35%.

compare.title: Sole vs joint ownership
compare.desc: Compares owning the home alone with joint spouse ownership ({shares}) using separate KRW 900M deductions. Joint owners who apply for the one-home special treatment are taxed like sole owners.
compare.note: Property tax is the same regardless of ownership (split by share). The joint one-home special treatment is applied for at the NTS each year from September 16–30 and continues while nothing changes. Per-person burden caps for joint owners are omitted here.

scenario.title: What if the assessed price changes?
scenario.label: Assessed price change
scenario.note: 2026 apartment assessed prices kept the 69% realization rate and only reflected market moves: +9.16% nationwide, +18.67% in Seoul (March draft). Base caps and burden caps can make actual increases smaller.

basics.title: Basics
items: Holding tax = property tax (local, July/September) + comprehensive real estate tax (national, December). Both are levied on whoever owns the home on June 1.
If the balance is paid on June 1 the buyer pays that year's tax; from June 2 the seller does.
Taxes use the official assessed price, not market price. Apartment prices are finalized at the end of April.
The rural special tax is 20% of the comprehensive tax. Property tax comes with the urban-area tax and local education tax.

property.title: Property tax
items: Tax base = assessed price × ratio. For 2026, one-home households: 43% (≤ KRW 300M), 44% (≤ 600M), 45% (above); other homes 60%.
Progressive 0.1–0.4%. One-home households with assessed price ≤ KRW 900M get 0.05–0.35%.
Urban-area tax (0.14% of base) and local education tax (20% of property tax) are billed together. The building regional resource facility tax is not included.
Base caps and burden caps limit yearly increases, so after a big price jump your bill may be lower than this estimate.
Paid half in July (16–31) and half in September (16–30).

jongbu.title: Comprehensive real estate tax
items: Tax base = (total assessed price − KRW 900M) × 60%. One-home households deduct KRW 1.2B.
Rates: up to 2 homes 0.5–2.7%; with 3+ homes the same up to a KRW 1.2B base, then 2.0–5.0%.
Property tax already paid on the same base is subtracted (double-taxation offset).
One-home credits: age 60 20%, 65 30%, 70 40%; holding 5 yrs 20%, 10 yrs 40%, 15 yrs 50%; combined max 80%.
Burden cap: if this year's property + comprehensive tax exceeds 150% of last year's, the excess is removed from the comprehensive tax.
Paid December 1–15. Above KRW 2.5M (about KRW 3M including the rural special tax), the excess over 2.5M (up to half above 5M) can be paid within six months.

tips.title: Good to know
items: Joint spouse owners of one home can choose separate KRW 900M deductions or the one-home special treatment (KRW 1.2B + credits). The older the owner and the longer the holding, the better the special treatment.
Temporary two homes, inherited homes and low-priced regional homes can be treated as one home on application (not modelled here).
One-home owners aged 60+ or holding 5+ years who meet income limits can defer comprehensive tax above KRW 1M (collateral required).
If the assessed price looks too high, comment during the March–April review or file an objection after publication.
If your bill differs, check Wetax/Hometax details for base caps, burden caps and reliefs.

reform.title: Possible changes from 2027 (government proposal, under review)
reform.body: The 2026 tax reform proposal would raise the comprehensive tax fair market value ratio to 70% from 2027 (80% in 2028 for regulated areas and 3+ homes), raise the owner-occupied one-home deduction to KRW 1.4B, raise the KRW 600M–1.2B bracket from 1.0% to 1.3%, and base credits on actual residence. It does not apply to the December 2026 bill and may change in the National Assembly.

items.q: When is the comprehensive tax billed and due?
items.a: The NTS bills in late November and payment is due December 1–15. You can check and pay on Hometax; above KRW 2.5M (about 3M with the rural special tax) part can be paid by June 15 next year.

items.q: Does a one-home owner with a KRW 1.2B assessed price pay comprehensive tax?
items.a: No. One-home households deduct KRW 1.2B, so they pay only property tax. Joint spouse owners with separate deductions pay nothing while each share is KRW 900M or less (e.g. KRW 1.8B split 50:50).

items.q: Isn't paying both taxes double taxation?
items.a: That is why property tax paid on the same base is subtracted from the comprehensive tax — the 'property tax offset' line above.

items.q: My assessed price jumped but my property tax rose less.
items.a: Property tax increases are limited by the base cap and burden cap. This calculator uses only this year's price, so your bill may be lower.

No. Separate deductions total KRW 1.8B but give no age/holding credits. Older or long-term owners may pay less with the one-home special treatment (KRW 1.2B + up to 80% credit), applied for each September 16–30. Check the comparison table.
No. Corporations get no deduction and pay a flat 2.7% (up to 2 homes) or 5.0% (3+ homes) with no credits or burden cap, so they are not covered.
